   163→
   164→// ReadTemporaryResult contains the result of reading a temporary checkpoint.
   165→type ReadTemporaryResult struct {
   166→	// CommitHash is the hash of the checkpoint commit

   169→	// TreeHash is the hash of the tree containing the checkpoint state

   171→
   172→	// SessionID is the session identifier from the commit trailer
   173→	SessionID string
   174→
   175→	// MetadataDir is the metadata directory path from the commit trailer
   176→	MetadataDir string
   177→
   178→	// Timestamp is when the checkpoint was created
   179→	Timestamp time.Time
   180→}

   182→// TemporaryInfo contains summary information about a shadow branch.
   183→type TemporaryInfo struct {
   184→	// BranchName is the full branch name (e.g., "entire/abc1234")
   185→	BranchName string
   186→
   187→	// BaseCommit is the short commit hash this branch is based on
   188→	BaseCommit string
   189→
   190→	// LatestCommit is the hash of the latest commit on the branch
   191→	LatestCommit plumbing.Hash
   192→
   193→	// SessionID is the session identifier from the latest commit

   195→
   196→	// Timestamp is when the latest checkpoint was created

   200→// WriteCommittedOptions contains options for writing a committed checkpoint.
   201→type WriteCommittedOptions struct {
   202→	// CheckpointID is the stable 12-hex-char identifier
   203→	CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
   204→
   205→	// SessionID is the session identifier
   206→	SessionID string
   207→
   208→	// Strategy is the name of the strategy that created this checkpoint
   209→	Strategy string
   210→
   211→	// Branch is the branch name where the checkpoint was created (empty if detached HEAD)
   212→	Branch string
   213→
   214→	// Transcript is the session transcript content (full.jsonl)
   215→	Transcript []byte
   216→
   217→	// Prompts contains user prompts from the session
   218→	Prompts []string
   219→
   220→	// FilesTouched are files modified during the session
   221→	FilesTouched []string
   222→
   223→	// CheckpointsCount is the number of checkpoints in this session
   224→	CheckpointsCount int
   225→
   226→	// EphemeralBranch is the shadow branch name (for manual-commit strategy)
   227→	EphemeralBranch string
   228→
   229→	// AuthorName is the name to use for commits
   230→	AuthorName string
   231→
   232→	// AuthorEmail is the email to use for commits
   233→	AuthorEmail string
   234→
   235→	// MetadataDir is a directory containing additional metadata files to copy
   236→	// If set, all files in this directory will be copied to the checkpoint path
   237→	// This is useful for copying task metadata files, subagent transcripts, etc.
   238→	MetadataDir string
   239→
   240→	// Task checkpoint fields (for task/subagent checkpoints)
   241→	IsTask    bool   // Whether this is a task checkpoint
   242→	ToolUseID string // Tool use ID for task checkpoints
   243→
   244→	// Additional task checkpoint fields for subagent checkpoints
   245→	AgentID                string // Subagent identifier
   246→	CheckpointUUID         string // UUID for transcript truncation when rewinding
   247→	TranscriptPath         string // Path to session transcript file (alternative to in-memory Transcript)
   248→	SubagentTranscriptPath string // Path to subagent's transcript file
   249→
   250→	// Incremental checkpoint fields
   251→	IsIncremental       bool   // Whether this is an incremental checkpoint
   252→	IncrementalSequence int    // Checkpoint sequence number
   253→	IncrementalType     string // Tool type that triggered this checkpoint
   254→	IncrementalData     []byte // Tool input payload for this checkpoint
   255→
   256→	// Commit message fields (used for task checkpoints)
   257→	CommitSubject string // Subject line for the metadata commit (overrides default)
   258→
   259→	// Agent identifies the agent that created this checkpoint (e.g., "Claude Code", "Cursor")
   260→	Agent types.AgentType
   261→
   262→	// Model is the LLM model used during the session (e.g., "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")
   263→	Model string
   264→
   265→	// TurnID correlates checkpoints from the same agent turn.
   266→	TurnID string
   267→
   268→	// Transcript position at checkpoint start - tracks what was added during this checkpoint
   269→	TranscriptIdentifierAtStart string // Last identifier when checkpoint started (UUID for Claude, message ID for Gemini)
   270→	CheckpointTranscriptStart   int    // Transcript line offset at start of this checkpoint's data
   271→
   272→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart is written to both CommittedMetadata.CheckpointTranscriptStart
   273→	// and the deprecated CommittedMetadata.TranscriptLinesAtStart for backward compatibility.
   274→
   275→	// TokenUsage contains the token usage for this checkpoint
   276→	TokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage
   277→
   278→	// SessionMetrics contains hook-provided session metrics (duration, turns, context usage)
   279→	SessionMetrics *SessionMetrics
   280→
   281→	// InitialAttribution is line-level attribution calculated at commit time
   282→	// comparing checkpoint tree (agent work) to committed tree (may include human edits)
   283→	InitialAttribution *InitialAttribution
   284→
   285→	// Summary is an optional AI-generated summary for this checkpoint.
   286→	// This field may be nil when:
   287→	//   - summarization is disabled in settings
   288→	//   - summary generation failed (non-blocking, logged as warning)
   289→	//   - the transcript was empty or too short to summarize
   290→	//   - the checkpoint predates the summarization feature
   291→	Summary *Summary
   292→}

   301→
   302→	// SessionID identifies which session slot to update within the checkpoint

   304→
   305→	// Transcript is the full session transcript (replaces existing)
   306→	Transcript []byte
   307→
   308→	// Prompts contains all user prompts (replaces existing)
   309→	Prompts []string
   310→
   311→	// Agent identifies the agent type (needed for transcript chunking)
   312→	Agent types.AgentType
   313→}

   407→// GetTranscriptStart returns the transcript line offset at which this checkpoint's data begins.
   408→// Returns 0 for new checkpoints (start from beginning). For data written by older CLI versions,
   409→// falls back to the deprecated TranscriptLinesAtStart field.
   410→func (m CommittedMetadata) GetTranscriptStart() int {
   411→	if m.CheckpointTranscriptStart > 0 {
   412→		return m.CheckpointTranscriptStart
   413→	}
   414→	return m.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   415→}

   427→// CheckpointSummary is the root-level metadata.json for a checkpoint.
   428→// It contains aggregated statistics from all sessions and a map of session IDs
   429→// to their file paths. Session-specific data (including initial_attribution)
   430→// is stored in the session's subdirectory metadata.json.
   431→//
   432→// Structure on entire/checkpoints/v1 branch:
   433→//
   434→//	<checkpoint-id[:2]>/<checkpoint-id[2:]>/
   435→//	├── metadata.json         # This CheckpointSummary
   436→//	├── 1/                    # First session
   437→//	│   ├── metadata.json     # Session-specific CommittedMetadata
   438→//	│   ├── full.jsonl
   439→//	│   ├── prompt.txt
   440→//	│   └── content_hash.txt
   441→//	├── 2/                    # Second session
   442→//	└── 3/                    # Third session...
   443→//
   444→//nolint:revive // Named CheckpointSummary to avoid conflict with existing Summary struct
   445→type CheckpointSummary struct {
   446→	CLIVersion       string             `json:"cli_version,omitempty"`

   449→	Branch           string             `json:"branch,omitempty"`
   450→	CheckpointsCount int                `json:"checkpoints_count"`
   451→	FilesTouched     []string           `json:"files_touched"`
   452→	Sessions         []SessionFilePaths `json:"sessions"`

   454→}

    45→// HashWorktreeID returns a short hash of the worktree identifier.

    52→// WriteTemporary writes a temporary checkpoint to a shadow branch.
    53→// Shadow branches are named entire/<base-commit-short-hash>.
    54→// Returns the result containing commit hash and whether it was skipped.
    55→// If the new tree hash matches the last checkpoint's tree hash, the checkpoint
    56→// is skipped to avoid duplicate commits (deduplication).
    57→func (s *GitStore) WriteTemporary(ctx context.Context, opts WriteTemporaryOptions) (WriteTemporaryResult, error) {
    58→	// Validate base commit - required for shadow branch naming
    59→	if opts.BaseCommit == "" {
    60→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, errors.New("BaseCommit is required for temporary checkpoint")
    61→	}
    62→
    63→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    64→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
    65→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid temporary checkpoint options: %w", err)
    66→	}
    67→
    68→	// Get shadow branch name
    69→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(opts.BaseCommit, opts.WorktreeID)
    70→
    71→	// Get or create shadow branch
    72→	parentHash, baseTreeHash, err := s.getOrCreateShadowBranch(shadowBranchName)
    73→	if err != nil {
    74→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get shadow branch: %w", err)
    75→	}
    76→
    77→	// Get the last checkpoint's tree hash for deduplication
    78→	var lastTreeHash plumbing.Hash
    79→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
    80→		if lastCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(parentHash); err == nil {
    81→			lastTreeHash = lastCommit.TreeHash
    82→		}
    83→	}
    84→
    85→	// Collect all files to include
    86→	var allFiles []string
    87→	var allDeletedFiles []string
    88→	if opts.IsFirstCheckpoint {
    89→		// For the first checkpoint, capture all changed files (modified tracked + untracked)
    90→		// using `git status --porcelain -z` which respects both repo and global .gitignore.
    91→		// This is much faster than filesystem walk. The base tree from HEAD already contains
    92→		// all unchanged tracked files. We also capture user's pre-existing deletions.
    93→		result, err := collectChangedFiles(ctx, s.repo)
    94→		if err != nil {
    95→			return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to collect changed files: %w", err)
    96→		}
    97→		allFiles = result.Changed
    98→		// Merge user's pre-existing deletions with agent's deletions
    99→		allDeletedFiles = result.Deleted
   100→		allDeletedFiles = append(allDeletedFiles, opts.DeletedFiles...)
   101→	} else {
   102→		// For subsequent checkpoints, only include modified/new files
   103→		allFiles = make([]string, 0, len(opts.ModifiedFiles)+len(opts.NewFiles))
   104→		allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.ModifiedFiles...)
   105→		allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.NewFiles...)
   106→		allDeletedFiles = opts.DeletedFiles
   107→	}
   108→
   109→	// Build tree with changes
   110→	treeHash, err := s.buildTreeWithChanges(ctx, baseTreeHash, allFiles, allDeletedFiles, opts.MetadataDir, opts.MetadataDirAbs)
   111→	if err != nil {
   112→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to build tree: %w", err)
   113→	}
   114→
   115→	// Deduplication: skip if tree hash matches the last checkpoint
   116→	if lastTreeHash != plumbing.ZeroHash && treeHash == lastTreeHash {
   117→		return WriteTemporaryResult{
   118→			CommitHash: parentHash,
   119→			Skipped:    true,
   120→		}, nil
   121→	}
   122→
   123→	// Create checkpoint commit with trailers
   124→	commitMsg := trailers.FormatShadowCommit(opts.CommitMessage, opts.MetadataDir, opts.SessionID)
   125→
   126→	commitHash, err := s.createCommit(treeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
   127→	if err != nil {
   128→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to create commit: %w", err)
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	// Update branch reference
   132→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   133→	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)
   134→	if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   135→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to update branch reference: %w", err)
   136→	}
   137→
   138→	return WriteTemporaryResult{
   139→		CommitHash: commitHash,
   140→		Skipped:    false,
   141→	}, nil
   142→}

   172→		SessionID:   sessionID,
   173→		MetadataDir: metadataDir,

   170→			sessionData.FilesTouched = filtered
   171→		}
   172→
   173→		if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) == 0 && !hadFilesBeforeFiltering {
   174→			sessionData.FilesTouched = make([]string, 0, len(committedFiles))
   175→			for f := range committedFiles {
   176→				sessionData.FilesTouched = append(sessionData.FilesTouched, f)
   177→			}
   178→		}
   179→	}
   180→
   181→	// Get checkpoint store
   182→	store, err := s.getCheckpointStore()
   183→	if err != nil {
   184→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get checkpoint store: %w", err)
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	// Get author info
   188→	authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   189→
   190→	// Determine attribution base commit
   191→	attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
   192→	if attrBase == "" {
   193→		attrBase = state.BaseCommit
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	attribution := calculateSessionAttributions(ctx, repo, ref, sessionData, state, attributionOpts{
   197→		headTree:              o.headTree,
   198→		repoDir:               o.repoDir,
   199→		attributionBaseCommit: attrBase,
   200→		headCommitHash:        o.headCommitHash,
   201→	})
   202→
   203→	// Get current branch name
   204→	branchName := GetCurrentBranchName(repo)
   205→
   206→	// Generate summary if enabled
   207→	var summary *cpkg.Summary
   208→	if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled(ctx) && len(sessionData.Transcript) > 0 {
   209→		summarizeCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "summarize")
   210→
   211→		var scopedTranscript []byte
   212→		switch state.AgentType {
   213→		case agent.AgentTypeGemini:
   214→			scoped, sliceErr := geminicli.SliceFromMessage(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   215→			if sliceErr != nil {
   216→				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "failed to scope Gemini transcript for summary",
   217→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   218→					slog.String("error", sliceErr.Error()))
   219→			}
   220→			scopedTranscript = scoped
   221→		case agent.AgentTypeOpenCode:
   222→			scoped, sliceErr := opencode.SliceFromMessage(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   223→			if sliceErr != nil {
   224→				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "failed to scope OpenCode transcript for summary",
   225→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   226→					slog.String("error", sliceErr.Error()))
   227→			}
   228→			scopedTranscript = scoped
   229→		case agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, agent.AgentTypeCursor, agent.AgentTypeFactoryAIDroid, agent.AgentTypeUnknown:
   230→			scopedTranscript = transcript.SliceFromLine(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   231→		}
   232→		if len(scopedTranscript) > 0 {
   233→			var err error
   234→			summary, err = summarize.GenerateFromTranscript(summarizeCtx, scopedTranscript, sessionData.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, nil)
   235→			if err != nil {
   236→				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "summary generation failed",
   237→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   238→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   239→			} else {
   240→				logging.Info(summarizeCtx, "summary generated",
   241→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID))
   242→			}
   243→		}
   244→	}
   245→
   246→	// Write checkpoint metadata using the checkpoint store
   247→	if err := store.WriteCommitted(ctx, cpkg.WriteCommittedOptions{
   248→		CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
   249→		SessionID:                   state.SessionID,
   250→		Strategy:                    StrategyNameManualCommit,
   251→		Branch:                      branchName,
   252→		Transcript:                  sessionData.Transcript,
   253→		Prompts:                     sessionData.Prompts,
   254→		FilesTouched:                sessionData.FilesTouched,
   255→		CheckpointsCount:            state.StepCount,
   256→		EphemeralBranch:             shadowBranchName,
   257→		AuthorName:                  authorName,
   258→		AuthorEmail:                 authorEmail,
   259→		Agent:                       state.AgentType,
   260→		Model:                       state.ModelName,
   261→		TurnID:                      state.TurnID,
   262→		TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: state.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
   263→		CheckpointTranscriptStart:   state.CheckpointTranscriptStart,
   264→		TokenUsage:                  sessionData.TokenUsage,
   265→		SessionMetrics:              buildSessionMetrics(state),
   266→		InitialAttribution:          attribution,
   267→		Summary:                     summary,
   268→	}); err != nil {
   269→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
   270→	}
   271→
   272→	return &CondenseResult{
   273→		CheckpointID:         checkpointID,
   274→		SessionID:            state.SessionID,
   275→		CheckpointsCount:     state.StepCount,
   276→		FilesTouched:         sessionData.FilesTouched,
   277→		Prompts:              sessionData.Prompts,
   278→		TotalTranscriptLines: sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
   279→		Transcript:           sessionData.Transcript,
   280→	}, nil
   281→}
   282→
   283→// buildSessionMetrics creates a SessionMetrics from session state if any metrics are available.
   284→// Returns nil if no hook-provided metrics exist (e.g., for agents that don't report them).
   285→func buildSessionMetrics(state *SessionState) *cpkg.SessionMetrics {
   286→	if state.SessionDurationMs == 0 && state.SessionTurnCount == 0 && state.ContextTokens == 0 && state.ContextWindowSize == 0 {
   287→		return nil
   288→	}
   289→	return &cpkg.SessionMetrics{
   290→		DurationMs:        state.SessionDurationMs,
   291→		TurnCount:         state.SessionTurnCount,
   292→		ContextTokens:     state.ContextTokens,
   293→		ContextWindowSize: state.ContextWindowSize,
   294→	}
   295→}

   297→func hasTokenUsageData(usage *agent.TokenUsage) bool {
   298→	if usage == nil {
   299→		return false
   300→	}

     3→import (
     4→	"context"

     7→	"github.com/entireio/cli/perf"

    10→// PrePush is called by the git pre-push hook before pushing to a remote.
    11→// It pushes the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch alongside the user's push.
    12→//
    13→// If a checkpoint_remote is configured in settings, the checkpoint branch is
    14→// pushed to the derived URL instead of the user's push remote. Trails always
    15→// go to the user's push remote.
    16→//
    17→// Configuration options (stored in .entire/settings.json under strategy_options):
    18→//   - push_sessions: false to disable automatic pushing of checkpoints
    19→//   - checkpoint_remote: {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"} to push to a separate repo
    20→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrePush(ctx context.Context, remote string) error {
    21→	// Load settings once for both remote resolution and push_sessions check
    22→	ps := resolvePushSettings(ctx, remote)
    23→
    24→	// Checkpoints: pushed to checkpoint URL if configured, otherwise to push remote
    25→	if !ps.pushDisabled {
    26→		_, pushCheckpointsSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_checkpoints_branch")
    27→		if err := pushBranchIfNeeded(ctx, ps.pushTarget(), paths.MetadataBranchName); err != nil {
    28→			pushCheckpointsSpan.RecordError(err)
    29→			pushCheckpointsSpan.End()
    30→			return err
    31→		}
    32→		pushCheckpointsSpan.End()
    33→	}
    34→
    35→	// Trails: always push to the user's push remote
    36→	_, pushTrailsSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_trails_branch")
    37→	err := pushBranchIfNeeded(ctx, ps.remote, paths.TrailsBranchName)
    38→	pushTrailsSpan.RecordError(err)
    39→	pushTrailsSpan.End()
    40→	return err
    41→}

1→// Package agent provides interfaces and types for integrating with coding agents.
     2→// It abstracts agent-specific behavior (hooks, log parsing, session storage) so that
     3→// the same Strategy implementations can work with any coding agent.
     4→package agent
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"io"
     9→
    10→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
    11→)
    12→
    13→// Agent defines the interface for interacting with a coding agent.
    14→// Each agent implementation (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, etc.) converts its
    15→// native format to the normalized types defined in this package.
    16→//
    17→// The interface is organized into three groups:
    18→//   - Identity (5 methods): Name, Type, Description, DetectPresence, ProtectedDirs
    19→//   - Transcript Storage (3 methods): ReadTranscript, ChunkTranscript, ReassembleTranscript
    20→//   - Legacy (6 methods): Will be moved to optional interfaces or removed in a future phase
    21→type Agent interface {
    22→	// --- Identity ---
    23→
    24→	// Name returns the agent registry key (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini")
    25→	Name() types.AgentName
    26→
    27→	// Type returns the agent type identifier (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI")
    28→	// This is stored in metadata and trailers.
    29→	Type() types.AgentType
    30→
    31→	// Description returns a human-readable description for UI
    32→	Description() string
    33→
    34→	// IsPreview returns whether the agent integration is in preview or stable
    35→	IsPreview() bool
    36→
    37→	// DetectPresence checks if this agent is configured in the repository
    38→	DetectPresence(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
    39→
    40→	// ProtectedDirs returns repo-root-relative directories that should never be
    41→	// modified or deleted during rewind or other destructive operations.
    42→	// Examples: [".claude"] for Claude, [".gemini"] for Gemini.
    43→	ProtectedDirs() []string
    44→
    45→	// --- Transcript Storage ---
    46→
    47→	// ReadTranscript reads the raw transcript bytes for a session.
    48→	ReadTranscript(sessionRef string) ([]byte, error)
    49→
    50→	// ChunkTranscript splits a transcript into chunks if it exceeds maxSize.
    51→	// Returns a slice of chunks. If the transcript fits in one chunk, returns single-element slice.
    52→	// The chunking is format-aware: JSONL splits at line boundaries, JSON splits message arrays.
    53→	ChunkTranscript(ctx context.Context, content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
    54→
    55→	// ReassembleTranscript combines chunks back into a single transcript.
    56→	// Handles format-specific reassembly (JSONL concatenation, JSON message merging).
    57→	ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
    58→
    59→	// --- Legacy methods (will move to optional interfaces in Phase 4) ---
    60→
    61→	// GetSessionID extracts session ID from hook input.
    62→	GetSessionID(input *HookInput) string
    63→
    64→	// GetSessionDir returns where agent stores session data for this repo.
    65→	GetSessionDir(repoPath string) (string, error)
    66→
    67→	// ResolveSessionFile returns the path to the session transcript file.
    68→	ResolveSessionFile(sessionDir, agentSessionID string) string
    69→
    70→	// ReadSession reads session data from agent's storage.
    71→	ReadSession(input *HookInput) (*AgentSession, error)
    72→
    73→	// WriteSession writes session data for resumption.
    74→	WriteSession(ctx context.Context, session *AgentSession) error
    75→
    76→	// FormatResumeCommand returns command to resume a session.
    77→	FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string
    78→}
    79→
    80→// HookSupport is implemented by agents with lifecycle hooks.
    81→// This optional interface allows agents like Claude Code and Cursor to
    82→// install and manage hooks that notify Entire of agent events.
    83→//
    84→// The interface is organized into two groups:
    85→//   - Hook Mapping (2 methods): HookNames, ParseHookEvent
    86→//   - Hook Management (3 methods): InstallHooks, UninstallHooks, AreHooksInstalled
    87→type HookSupport interface {
    88→	Agent
    89→
    90→	// HookNames returns the hook verbs this agent supports.
    91→	// These become subcommands under `entire hooks <agent>`.
    92→	// e.g., ["stop", "user-prompt-submit", "session-start", "session-end"]
    93→	HookNames() []string
    94→
    95→	// ParseHookEvent translates an agent-native hook into a normalized lifecycle Event.
    96→	// Returns nil if the hook has no lifecycle significance (e.g., pass-through hooks).
    97→	// This is the core contribution surface for new agent implementations.
    98→	ParseHookEvent(ctx context.Context, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*Event, error)
    99→
   100→	// InstallHooks installs agent-specific hooks.
   101→	// If localDev is true, hooks point to local development build.
   102→	// If force is true, removes existing Entire hooks before installing.
   103→	// Returns the number of hooks installed.
   104→	InstallHooks(ctx context.Context, localDev bool, force bool) (int, error)
   105→
   106→	// UninstallHooks removes installed hooks
   107→	UninstallHooks(ctx context.Context) error
   108→
   109→	// AreHooksInstalled checks if hooks are currently installed
   110→	AreHooksInstalled(ctx context.Context) bool
   111→}
   112→
   113→// FileWatcher is implemented by agents that use file-based detection.
   114→// Agents like Aider that don't support hooks can use file watching
   115→// to detect session activity.
   116→type FileWatcher interface {
   117→	Agent
   118→
   119→	// GetWatchPaths returns paths to watch for session changes
   120→	GetWatchPaths() ([]string, error)
   121→
   122→	// OnFileChange handles a detected file change and returns session info
   123→	OnFileChange(path string) (*SessionChange, error)
   124→}
   125→
   126→// TranscriptAnalyzer provides format-specific transcript parsing.
   127→// Agents that implement this get richer checkpoints (transcript-derived file lists,
   128→// prompts, summaries). Agents that don't still participate in the checkpoint lifecycle
   129→// via git-status-based file detection and raw transcript storage.
   130→type TranscriptAnalyzer interface {
   131→	Agent
   132→
   133→	// GetTranscriptPosition returns the current position (length) of a transcript.
   134→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), this is the line count.
   135→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), this is the message count.
   136→	// Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or is empty.
   137→	GetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error)
   138→
   139→	// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given offset.
   140→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), offset is the starting line number.
   141→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), offset is the starting message index.
   142→	// Returns:
   143→	//   - files: list of file paths modified by the agent (from Write/Edit tools)
   144→	//   - currentPosition: the current position (line count or message count)
   145→	//   - error: any error encountered during reading
   146→	ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error)
   147→}
   148→
   149→// PromptExtractor extracts user prompts from a transcript file.
   150→// Used as a fallback when prompt data isn't captured via hooks (e.g., Factory AI
   151→// Droid's exec mode doesn't fire UserPromptSubmit).
   152→type PromptExtractor interface {
   153→	Agent
   154→
   155→	// ExtractPrompts returns user prompts from the transcript starting at the given offset.
   156→	ExtractPrompts(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) ([]string, error)
   157→}
   158→
   159→// TranscriptPreparer is called before ReadTranscript to handle agent-specific
   160→// flush/sync requirements (e.g., Claude Code's async transcript writing).
   161→// The framework calls PrepareTranscript before ReadTranscript if implemented.
   162→type TranscriptPreparer interface {
   163→	Agent
   164→
   165→	// PrepareTranscript ensures the transcript is ready to read.
   166→	// For Claude Code, this waits for the async transcript flush to complete.
   167→	PrepareTranscript(ctx context.Context, sessionRef string) error
   168→}
   169→
   170→// TokenCalculator provides token usage calculation for a session.
   171→// The framework calls this during step save and checkpoint if implemented.
   172→type TokenCalculator interface {
   173→	Agent
   174→
   175→	// CalculateTokenUsage computes token usage from the transcript starting at the given offset.
   176→	CalculateTokenUsage(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int) (*TokenUsage, error)
   177→}
   178→
   179→// TextGenerator is an optional interface for agents whose CLI supports
   180→// non-interactive text generation (e.g., claude --print).
   181→// Used for AI-powered metadata generation (trail titles, summaries).
   182→type TextGenerator interface {
   183→	Agent
   184→
   185→	// GenerateText sends a prompt to the agent's CLI and returns the raw text response.
   186→	// model is a hint (e.g., "haiku", "sonnet"). Implementations may ignore if not applicable.
   187→	GenerateText(ctx context.Context, prompt string, model string) (string, error)
   188→}
   189→
   190→// HookResponseWriter is implemented by agents that support structured hook responses.
   191→// Agents that implement this can output messages (e.g., banners) to the user via
   192→// the agent's response protocol. For example, Claude Code outputs JSON with a
   193→// systemMessage field to stdout. Agents that don't implement this will silently
   194→// skip hook response output.
   195→type HookResponseWriter interface {
   196→	Agent
   197→
   198→	// WriteHookResponse outputs a message to the user via the agent's hook response protocol.
   199→	WriteHookResponse(message string) error
   200→}
   201→
   202→// TestOnly is implemented by agents that exist solely for testing (e.g., the Vogon canary agent).
   203→// These agents are excluded from the user-facing agent selection in `entire enable`.
   204→type TestOnly interface {
   205→	Agent
   206→	IsTestOnly() bool
   207→}
   208→
   209→// SubagentAwareExtractor provides methods for extracting files and tokens including subagents.
   210→// Agents that support spawning subagents (like Claude Code's Task tool) should implement this
   211→// to ensure subagent contributions are included in checkpoints.
   212→type SubagentAwareExtractor interface {
   213→	Agent
   214→
   215→	// ExtractAllModifiedFiles extracts files modified by both the main agent and any spawned subagents.
   216→	// The subagentsDir parameter specifies where subagent transcripts are stored.
   217→	// Returns a deduplicated list of all modified file paths.
   218→	ExtractAllModifiedFiles(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int, subagentsDir string) ([]string, error)
   219→
   220→	// CalculateTotalTokenUsage computes token usage including all spawned subagents.
   221→	// The subagentsDir parameter specifies where subagent transcripts are stored.
   222→	CalculateTotalTokenUsage(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int, subagentsDir string) (*TokenUsage, error)
   223→}

    94→// GetCommitLinking returns the effective commit linking mode.
    95→// Returns the explicit value if set, otherwise defaults to "prompt"
    96→// to preserve existing user behavior.
    97→func (s *EntireSettings) GetCommitLinking() string {

    99→		return s.CommitLinking

   101→	return CommitLinkingPrompt

   103→
   104→// Load loads the Entire settings from .entire/settings.json,
   105→// then applies any overrides from .entire/settings.local.json if it exists.
   106→// Returns default settings if neither file exists.
   107→// Works correctly from any subdirectory within the repository.
   108→func Load(ctx context.Context) (*EntireSettings, error) {
   109→	// Get absolute paths for settings files
   110→	settingsFileAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(ctx, EntireSettingsFile)
   111→	if err != nil {
   112→		settingsFileAbs = EntireSettingsFile // Fallback to relative
   113→	}
   114→	localSettingsFileAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(ctx, EntireSettingsLocalFile)
   115→	if err != nil {
   116→		localSettingsFileAbs = EntireSettingsLocalFile // Fallback to relative
   117→	}
   118→
   119→	// Load base settings
   120→	settings, err := loadFromFile(settingsFileAbs)
   121→	if err != nil {
   122→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading settings file: %w", err)
   123→	}
   124→
   125→	// Apply local overrides if they exist
   126→	localData, err := os.ReadFile(localSettingsFileAbs) //nolint:gosec // path is from AbsPath or constant
   127→	if err != nil {
   128→		if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   129→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading local settings file: %w", err)
   130→		}
   131→		// Local file doesn't exist, continue without overrides
   132→	} else {
   133→		if err := mergeJSON(settings, localData); err != nil {
   134→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merging local settings: %w", err)
   135→		}
   136→	}
   137→
   138→	return settings, nil
   139→}
   140→
   141→// LoadFromFile loads settings from a specific file path without merging local overrides.
   142→// Returns default settings if the file doesn't exist.
   143→// Use this when you need to display individual settings files separately.
   144→func LoadFromFile(filePath string) (*EntireSettings, error) {
   145→	return loadFromFile(filePath)
   146→}
   147→

   190→	// Default or with session filter: show list view (optionally filtered by session)
   191→	return runExplainBranchWithFilter(ctx, w, noPager, sessionID)
   192→}

    67→func runResume(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, branchName string, force bool) error {
    68→	w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
    69→	errW := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
    70→
    71→	// Check if we're already on this branch
    72→	currentBranch, err := GetCurrentBranch(ctx)
    73→	if err == nil && currentBranch == branchName {
    74→		// Already on the branch, skip checkout
    75→		return resumeFromCurrentBranch(ctx, w, errW, branchName, force)
    76→	}
    77→
    78→	// Check if branch exists locally
    79→	exists, err := BranchExistsLocally(ctx, branchName)
    80→	if err != nil {
    81→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check branch: %w", err)
    82→	}
    83→
    84→	if !exists {
    85→		// Branch doesn't exist locally, check if it exists on remote
    86→		remoteExists, err := BranchExistsOnRemote(ctx, branchName)
    87→		if err != nil {
    88→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote branch: %w", err)
    89→		}
    90→
    91→		if !remoteExists {
    92→			return fmt.Errorf("branch '%s' not found locally or on origin", branchName)
    93→		}
    94→
    95→		// Ask user if they want to fetch from remote
    96→		shouldFetch, err := promptFetchFromRemote(branchName)
    97→		if err != nil {
    98→			return err
    99→		}
   100→		if !shouldFetch {
   101→			return nil
   102→		}
   103→
   104→		// Fetch and checkout the remote branch
   105→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Fetching branch '%s' from origin...\n", branchName)
   106→		if err := FetchAndCheckoutRemoteBranch(ctx, branchName); err != nil {
   107→			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Error: failed to checkout branch: %v\n", err)
   108→			return NewSilentError(errors.New("failed to checkout branch"))
   109→		}
   110→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "✓ Switched to branch %s\n", branchName)
   111→	} else {
   112→		// Branch exists locally, check for uncommitted changes before checkout
   113→		hasChanges, err := HasUncommittedChanges(ctx)
   114→		if err != nil {
   115→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
   116→		}
   117→		if hasChanges {
   118→			return errors.New("you have uncommitted changes. Please commit or stash them first")
   119→		}
   120→
   121→		// Checkout the branch
   122→		if err := CheckoutBranch(ctx, branchName); err != nil {
   123→			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Error: failed to checkout branch: %v\n", err)
   124→			return NewSilentError(errors.New("failed to checkout branch"))
   125→		}
   126→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "✓ Switched to branch %s\n", branchName)
   127→	}
   128→
   129→	return resumeFromCurrentBranch(ctx, w, errW, branchName, force)
   130→}

   132→func resumeFromCurrentBranch(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, branchName string, force bool) error {
   133→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume")
   134→
   135→	repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
   136→	if err != nil {
   137→		return fmt.Errorf("not a git repository: %w", err)
   138→	}
   139→
   140→	// Find a commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, looking at branch-only commits
   141→	result, err := findBranchCheckpoints(repo, branchName)
   142→	if err != nil {
   143→		return err
   144→	}
   145→	if len(result.checkpointIDs) == 0 {
   146→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "No Entire checkpoint found on branch '%s'\n", branchName)
   147→		return nil
   148→	}
   149→
   150→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "found checkpoint(s) on branch",
   151→		slog.String("branch", branchName),
   152→		slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(result.checkpointIDs)),
   153→		slog.String("commit", result.commitHash[:7]),
   154→		slog.Bool("newer_commits_exist", result.newerCommitsExist),
   155→	)
   156→
   157→	// If there are newer commits without checkpoints, ask for confirmation.
   158→	// Merge commits (e.g., from merging main) don't count as "work" and are skipped silently.
   159→	if result.newerCommitsExist && !force {
   160→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found checkpoint in an older commit.\n")
   161→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "There are %d newer commit(s) on this branch without checkpoints.\n", result.newerCommitCount)
   162→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Checkpoint from: %s %s\n\n", result.commitHash[:7], firstLine(result.commitMessage))
   163→
   164→		shouldResume, err := promptResumeFromOlderCheckpoint()
   165→		if err != nil {
   166→			return err
   167→		}
   168→		if !shouldResume {
   169→			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Resume cancelled.\n")
   170→			return nil
   171→		}
   172→	}
   173→
   174→	checkpointID := result.checkpointIDs[0]
   175→
   176→	// Multiple checkpoints (squash merge): resolve latest by CreatedAt timestamp.
   177→	// resolveLatestCheckpoint also returns the metadata tree so we can reuse it
   178→	// for the ReadCheckpointMetadata call below without a redundant lookup.
   179→	var metadataTree *object.Tree
   180→	var freshRepo *git.Repository
   181→	if len(result.checkpointIDs) > 1 {
   182→		latest, tree, latestRepo, err := resolveLatestCheckpoint(ctx, result.checkpointIDs)
   183→		if err != nil {
   184→			// No metadata available — nothing to resume from
   185→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "resolveLatestCheckpoint failed",
   186→				slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(result.checkpointIDs)),
   187→				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   188→			)
   189→			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s but metadata is not available\n",
   190→				len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7])
   191→			return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, result.checkpointIDs[0])
   192→		}
   193→		skipped := len(result.checkpointIDs) - 1
   194→		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s, resuming from the latest (%d older checkpoints skipped)\n",
   195→			len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7], skipped)
   196→		checkpointID = latest
   197→		metadataTree = tree
   198→		freshRepo = latestRepo
   199→	}
   200→

    39→// hasTTY checks if /dev/tty is available for interactive prompts.
    40→// Returns false when running as an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
    41→//
    42→// In test environments, ENTIRE_TEST_TTY overrides the real check:
    43→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 → simulate human (TTY available)
    44→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 → simulate agent (no TTY)
    45→func hasTTY() bool {
    46→	if v := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"); v != "" {
    47→		return v == "1"
    48→	}
    49→
    50→	// Gemini CLI sets GEMINI_CLI=1 when running shell commands.
    51→	// Gemini subprocesses may have access to the user's TTY, but they can't
    52→	// actually respond to interactive prompts. Treat them as non-TTY.
    53→	// See: https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/shell/
    54→	if os.Getenv("GEMINI_CLI") != "" {
    55→		return false
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	// Copilot CLI sets COPILOT_CLI=1 when running hook subprocesses (v0.0.421+).
    59→	// Like Gemini, the subprocess may inherit the user's TTY but can't respond
    60→	// to interactive prompts.
    61→	if os.Getenv("COPILOT_CLI") != "" {
    62→		return false
    63→	}
    64→
    65→	// GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 disables git's own terminal prompts.
    66→	// Factory AI Droid (and other non-interactive environments like CI) set this.
    67→	// Since we run as a git hook, respect it — if the environment doesn't want
    68→	// git prompting, our hook shouldn't prompt either.
    69→	if os.Getenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT") == "0" {
    70→		return false
    71→	}
    72→
    73→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    74→	if err != nil {
    75→		return false
    76→	}
    77→	_ = tty.Close()
    78→	return true
    79→}
    80→
    81→// ttyResult represents the outcome of a TTY confirmation prompt.
    82→type ttyResult int
    83→
    84→const (
    85→	ttyResultLink       ttyResult = iota // Link: add the checkpoint trailer
    86→	ttyResultSkip                        // Skip: don't add the trailer
    87→	ttyResultLinkAlways                  // Link and remember: add trailer + save "always" preference
    88→)
    89→
    90→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user via /dev/tty whether to link a commit to session context.
    91→// This requires a controlling terminal — callers must check hasTTY() first and handle
    92→// the no-TTY case (agent subprocesses, CI) themselves.
    93→//
    94→// header is displayed as the first line (e.g., "Entire: Active Claude Code session").
    95→// detail lines are displayed indented below the header.
    96→func askConfirmTTY(header string, details []string, prompt string, defaultYes bool) ttyResult {
    97→	defaultResult := ttyResultSkip
    98→	if defaultYes {
    99→		defaultResult = ttyResultLink
   100→	}
   101→
   102→	// In test mode, don't try to interact with the real TTY — just use the default.
   103→	// ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 simulates "a human is present" for the hasTTY() check
   104→	// but we can't actually read from the TTY in tests.
   105→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY") != "" {
   106→		return defaultResult
   107→	}
   108→
   109→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing.
   110→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
   111→	// (e.g., human runs git commit -m where stdin is not a pipe).
   112→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
   113→	if err != nil {
   114→		return defaultResult
   115→	}
   116→	defer tty.Close()
   117→
   118→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
   119→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", header)
   120→	for _, line := range details {
   121→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "  %s\n", line)
   122→	}
   123→
   124→	// Show prompt with option descriptions
   125→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", prompt)
   126→	if defaultYes {
   127→		fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
   128→	} else {
   129→		fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [y]es / [N]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
   130→	}
   131→
   132→	// Read response
   133→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
   134→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
   135→	if err != nil {
   136→		return defaultResult
   137→	}
   138→
   139→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
   140→	switch response {
   141→	case "y", "yes":
   142→		return ttyResultLink
   143→	case "n", "no":
   144→		return ttyResultSkip
   145→	case "a", "always":
   146→		return ttyResultLinkAlways
   147→	default:
   148→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
   149→		return defaultResult
   150→	}
   151→}

   153→// saveCommitLinkingAlways persists commit_linking = "always" to settings.local.json.
   154→// Uses raw JSON merge to set only the commit_linking field without affecting other
   155→// fields. This avoids writing unintended defaults (e.g., enabled: true) when the
   156→// local settings file doesn't exist yet.
   157→func saveCommitLinkingAlways(ctx context.Context) error {
   158→	localPath, err := paths.AbsPath(ctx, settings.EntireSettingsLocalFile)
   159→	if err != nil {
   160→		return fmt.Errorf("resolving local settings path: %w", err)
   161→	}
   162→
   163→	// Read existing file as raw JSON map to preserve all existing fields.
   164→	// If the file doesn't exist, start with an empty map so we only write commit_linking.
   165→	var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
   166→	data, readErr := os.ReadFile(localPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from AbsPath
   167→	if readErr == nil {
   168→		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
   169→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing local settings: %w", err)
   170→		}
   171→	} else if !os.IsNotExist(readErr) {
   172→		return fmt.Errorf("reading local settings: %w", readErr)
   173→	}
   174→	if raw == nil {
   175→		raw = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
   176→	}
   177→
   178→	raw["commit_linking"] = json.RawMessage(`"` + settings.CommitLinkingAlways + `"`)
   179→
   180→	out, err := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
   181→	if err != nil {
   182→		return fmt.Errorf("marshaling local settings: %w", err)
   183→	}
   184→	out = append(out, '\n')
   185→
   186→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(localPath), 0o750); err != nil {
   187→		return fmt.Errorf("creating settings directory: %w", err)
   188→	}
   189→	//nolint:gosec // G306: settings file is config, not secrets; 0o644 is appropriate
   190→	if err := os.WriteFile(localPath, out, 0o644); err != nil {
   191→		return fmt.Errorf("writing local settings: %w", err)
   192→	}
   193→	return nil
   194→}

   196→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
   197→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
   198→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
   199→
   200→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(_ context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error { //nolint:unparam // error return is part of the hook contract; callers check it
   201→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
   202→	if err != nil {
   203→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   204→	}
   205→
   206→	message := string(content)
   207→
   208→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   209→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
   210→		// No trailer, nothing to do
   211→		return nil
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
   215→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
   216→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
   217→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
   218→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   219→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   220→		}
   221→	}
   222→
   223→	return nil
   224→}
   225→
   226→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   227→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   228→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   229→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   230→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   231→		// Skip empty lines
   232→		if trimmed == "" {
   233→			continue
   234→		}
   235→		// Skip comment lines
   236→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   237→			continue
   238→		}
   239→		// Skip our trailer line
   240→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   241→			continue
   242→		}
   243→		// Found user content
   244→		return true
   245→	}
   246→	return false
   247→}
   248→
   249→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   250→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   251→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   252→	var result []string
   253→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   254→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   255→			result = append(result, line)
   256→		}
   257→	}
   258→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   259→}

   261→// isGitSequenceOperation checks if git is currently in the middle of a rebase,
   262→// cherry-pick, or revert operation. During these operations, commits are being
   263→// replayed and should not be linked to agent sessions.
   264→//
   265→// Detects:
   266→//   - rebase: .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ directories
   267→//   - cherry-pick: .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD file
   268→//   - revert: .git/REVERT_HEAD file
   269→func isGitSequenceOperation(ctx context.Context) bool {
   270→	// Get git directory (handles worktrees and relative paths correctly)
   271→	gitDir, err := GetGitDir(ctx)
   272→	if err != nil {
   273→		return false // Can't determine, assume not in sequence operation
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Check for rebase state directories
   277→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-merge")); err == nil {
   278→		return true
   279→	}
   280→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   281→		return true
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   285→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   286→		return true
   287→	}
   288→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   289→		return true
   290→	}
   291→
   292→	return false
   293→}

   295→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   296→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   297→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   298→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   299→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   300→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.

300→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   301→//
   302→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   303→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   304→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   305→//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
   306→//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from LastCheckpointID
   307→//
   308→
   309→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(ctx context.Context, commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   310→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   311→

   393→			slog.String("source", source),
   394→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   395→		)

   397→	}

   500→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   501→	)

   503→	// Write updated message back
   504→	_, writeCommitMessageSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_commit_message")

   515→// handleAmendCommitMsg handles the prepare-commit-msg hook for amend operations
   516→// (source="commit"). It preserves existing trailers or restores from LastCheckpointID.
   517→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) handleAmendCommitMsg(ctx context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error {
   518→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   519→	// Read current commit message
   520→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   521→	if err != nil {
   522→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   523→	}
   524→
   525→	message := string(content)
   526→
   527→	// If message already has a trailer, keep it unchanged
   528→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   529→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend preserves existing trailer",
   530→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   531→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   532→		)
   533→		return nil
   534→	}
   535→
   536→	// No trailer in message — check if any session has LastCheckpointID to restore
   537→	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   538→	if err != nil {
   539→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   540→	}
   541→
   542→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(ctx, worktreePath)
   543→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   544→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // No sessions - nothing to restore
   545→	}
   546→
   547→	// For amend, HEAD^ is the commit being amended, and HEAD is where we are now.
   548→	// We need to match sessions whose BaseCommit equals HEAD (the commit being amended
   549→	// was created from this base). This prevents stale sessions from injecting
   550→	// unrelated checkpoint IDs.
   551→	repo, repoErr := OpenRepository(ctx)
   552→	if repoErr != nil {
   553→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   554→	}
   555→	head, headErr := repo.Head()
   556→	if headErr != nil {
   557→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   558→	}
   559→	currentHead := head.Hash().String()
   560→
   561→	// Find first matching session with LastCheckpointID to restore.
   562→	// LastCheckpointID is set after condensation completes.
   563→	for _, state := range sessions {
   564→		if state.BaseCommit != currentHead {
   565→			continue
   566→		}
   567→		if state.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   568→			continue
   569→		}
   570→		cpID := state.LastCheckpointID
   571→		source := "LastCheckpointID"
   572→
   573→		// Restore the trailer
   574→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, cpID)
   575→		if writeErr := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); writeErr != nil { //nolint:gosec // path from git hook arg
   576→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   577→		}
   578→
   579→		logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: restored trailer on amend",
   580→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   581→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpID.String()),
   582→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   583→			slog.String("source", source),
   584→		)
   585→		return nil
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	// No checkpoint ID found - leave message unchanged
   589→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend with no checkpoint to restore",
   590→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   591→	)
   592→	return nil
   593→}

   595→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   596→// Uses the session state machine to determine what action to take per session:
   597→//   - ACTIVE → condense immediately (each commit gets its own checkpoint)
   598→//   - IDLE → condense immediately
   599→//   - ENDED → condense if files touched, discard if empty
   600→//
   601→// After condensation for ACTIVE sessions, remaining uncommitted files are
   602→// carried forward to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.
   603→//
   604→// Shadow branches are only deleted when ALL sessions sharing the branch are non-active
   605→// and were condensed during this PostCommit.
   606→
   607→// postCommitActionHandler implements session.ActionHandler for PostCommit.
   608→// Each session in the loop gets its own handler with per-session context.
   609→// Handler methods use the *State parameter from ApplyTransition (same pointer
   610→// as the state being transitioned) rather than capturing state separately.
   611→type postCommitActionHandler struct {
   612→	s                      *ManualCommitStrategy
   613→	ctx                    context.Context
   614→	repo                   *git.Repository
   615→	checkpointID           id.CheckpointID
   616→	head                   *plumbing.Reference
   617→	commit                 *object.Commit
   618→	newHead                string
   619→	repoDir                string
   620→	shadowBranchName       string
   621→	shadowBranchesToDelete map[string]struct{}
   622→	committedFileSet       map[string]struct{}
   623→	hasNew                 bool
   624→	filesTouchedBefore     []string

   626→	// Cached git objects — resolved once per PostCommit invocation to avoid
   627→	// redundant reads across filesOverlapWithContent, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges,
   628→	// CondenseSession, and calculateSessionAttributions.
   629→	headTree   *object.Tree        // HEAD commit tree (shared across all sessions)
   630→	parentTree *object.Tree        // HEAD's first parent tree (shared, nil for initial commits)
   631→	shadowRef  *plumbing.Reference // Per-session shadow branch ref (nil if branch doesn't exist)
   632→	shadowTree *object.Tree        // Per-session shadow commit tree (nil if branch doesn't exist)
   633→
   634→	// Output: set by handler methods, read by caller after TransitionAndLog.
   635→	condensed bool
   636→}

   639→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint")
   640→	shouldCondense := h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive(), state.LastInteractionTime)
   641→
   642→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondense decision",
   643→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   644→		slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   645→		slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   646→		slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   647→		slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   648→	)

   650→	if shouldCondense {
   651→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.ctx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet, condenseOpts{

   653→			headTree:       h.headTree,
   654→			repoDir:        h.repoDir,
   655→			headCommitHash: h.newHead,

Perfect! Now I have thoroughly explored the codebase. Let me prepare a comprehensive summary document:

## Comprehensive Checkpoint System Architecture Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the Entire CLI codebase, here's a detailed understanding of the current checkpoint system:

### 1. **Checkpoint Storage Layer** (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`)

**Core Types & Interfaces:**
- `Store` interface (in `checkpoint.go`) - abstracts read/write operations for both temporary and committed checkpoints
- `GitStore` - implements the Store interface, wrapping a git.Repository
- Two checkpoint types: `Temporary` (shadow branches) and `Committed` (entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)

**Temporary Checkpoints (Shadow Branches):**
- Location: Shadow branches named `entire/<base-commit-short-hash>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
- Used for intra-session rewind
- Written by `WriteTemporary()` in `temporary.go`
- Contain full state: code + metadata in git tree
- Deduplication: skipped if tree hash matches previous checkpoint
- Include worktree ID hash to support multiple worktrees per repo

**Committed Checkpoints (`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch):**
- Location: Sharded paths `<checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/`
- Contain metadata + commit reference
- Written by `WriteCommitted()` in `committed.go`
- Multi-session support: sessions stored in numbered subdirectories (0/, 1/, 2/, etc.)
- Structure per checkpoint:
  ```
  <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
  ├── metadata.json         # CheckpointSummary (aggregated stats)
  ├── 1/                    # First session
  │   ├── metadata.json     # CommittedMetadata (session-specific)
  │   ├── full.jsonl        # Transcript (chunked if large)
  │   ├── prompt.txt        # User prompts
  │   └── content_hash.txt  # SHA256 of transcript
  ├── 2/                    # Second session
  └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/  # Task checkpoints (optional)
      ├── checkpoint.json
      └── agent-<id>.jsonl
  ```

### 2. **Condensation Logic** (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go`)

**CondenseSession Function:**
- Converts temporary checkpoint (shadow branch) → committed checkpoint (metadata branch)
- Checkpoint ID: 12-hex-char stable identifier from `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
- Process:
  1. Extracts session data from shadow branch or live transcript
  2. Filters files_touched to only committed files (1:1 model)
  3. Calculates attribution (agent vs human lines)
  4. Generates AI summary if enabled
  5. Writes to `entire/checkpoints/v1` via `store.WriteCommitted()`

**Data Extraction:**
- `extractSessionData()` - reads from shadow branch tree
- `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript()` - reads live file for mid-session commits
- Falls back to live file if shadow branch is stale
- Handles agent-specific transcript formats (JSONL for Claude Code, JSON for Gemini/OpenCode)

**Token Usage:**
- Calculated at condensation time from transcript portion (CheckpointTranscriptStart)
- Backfilled from full transcript for agents like Copilot CLI that write post-hook

**Prompts:**
- Source of truth: `prompt.txt` in shadow branch
- Fallback: read from filesystem session metadata
- Fallback: extracted from transcript if neither exists

### 3. **Push Logic** (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go`)

**PrePush Hook:**
- Called before pushing to remote
- Pushes two branches:
  1. `entire/checkpoints/v1` - metadata (to checkpoint_remote if configured)
  2. `entire/trails/v1` - trail metadata (always to user's push remote)
- Settings:
  - `push_sessions`: false to disable checkpoint pushing
  - `checkpoint_remote`: {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"} for separate repo

### 4. **Transcript Handling**

**Current Approach (Read-as-is):**
- Transcripts are copied as-is from agent session directories
- No parsing/transformation at storage time
- Agent-agnostic for most cases

**Format Support:**
- **Claude Code**: JSONL format (one message per line)
- **Gemini CLI**: JSON with messages array
- **OpenCode**: JSON export format with info + messages
- **Cursor**: JSONL variant
- **Factory AI Droid**: Custom envelope format with normalized parsing
- **External Agents**: Protocol delegates to binary via `ReadTranscript` subcommand

**Transcript Chunking:**
- Large transcripts are split into chunks before storage
- `agent.ChunkTranscript()` - format-aware splitting
- Stored as `full_0.jsonl`, `full_1.jsonl`, etc.
- Agent-specific chunk reassembly via `ReassembleTranscript()`

**Transcript Lifecycle:**
- Stored in shadow branch during session
- Copied to `entire/checkpoints/v1` at condensation
- `full.jsonl` (or legacy `full.log`) for compatibility
- Read for summarization, explanation, resume

### 5. **Agent Interface** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go`)

**Core Agent Interface:**
- `Name()`, `Type()`, `Description()`, `DetectPresence()`, `ProtectedDirs()`
- `ReadTranscript()`, `ChunkTranscript()`, `ReassembleTranscript()`
- Legacy: `GetSessionID()`, `GetSessionDir()`, `ResolveSessionFile()`, `ReadSession()`, `WriteSession()`, `FormatResumeCommand()`

**Optional Interfaces (Capabilities):**
- `HookSupport` - lifecycle hooks (Claude Code, Cursor)
- `TranscriptAnalyzer` - format-specific parsing (extract files, positions)
- `PromptExtractor` - extract user prompts fallback
- `TokenCalculator` - token usage from transcript
- `TranscriptPreparer` - async flush (Claude Code waits for flush)
- `SubagentAwareExtractor` - task/subagent file extraction

**External Agents** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/`)
- Plugin system via `entire-agent-<name>` binaries on PATH
- Protocol: subcommand-based with JSON stdin/stdout
- Protocol version 1
- Discovered and registered dynamically
- All operations delegated to binary (read-transcript, chunk-transcript, parse-hook, etc.)

### 6. **Current Ref Structure**

**User-facing branches:**
- Main working branches (main, feature branches, etc.)
- Commits decorated with `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer

**CLI-created branches:**
- `entire/checkpoints/v1` - Orphan branch storing metadata/transcripts (pushed to checkpoint_remote)
- `entire/trails/v1` - Orphan branch storing trail metadata (pushed to user's remote)
- `entire/<base-commit>-<worktreeHash>` - Shadow branches (ephemeral, not pushed)

**Commit Trailers:**

On user commits:
- `Entire-Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` - Links to metadata on entire/checkpoints/v1

On shadow branch commits:
- `Entire-Session: <session-id>`
- `Entire-Metadata: <path>`
- `Entire-Task-Metadata: <path>`
- `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit`

On metadata branch commits:
- Subject: `Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` (or custom for task checkpoints)
- `Entire-Session: <session-id>`
- `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit`
- `Entire-Agent: <agent-name>` (optional)
- `Ephemeral-branch: <branch>` (optional)

### 7. **Settings** (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`)

**Current strategy_options:**
- `push_sessions: false` - disable checkpoint pushing
- `checkpoint_remote: {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` - push checkpoints to separate repo
- Future: `strategy` field (deprecated, kept for tolerance)

**Other Settings:**
- `enabled`, `local_dev`, `log_level`, `absolute_git_hook_path`, `telemetry`, `redaction`, `commit_linking`, `external_agents`

### 8. **Resume Command** (`cmd/entire/cli/resume.go`)

**Functionality:**
- Finds most recent commit with `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
- Resolves checkpoint ID from trailer
- Reads checkpoint metadata from `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- Restores session log if missing locally
- Returns resume command for agent

**Multi-checkpoint Resolution:**
- If multiple checkpoints exist for same commit, picks latest by CreatedAt timestamp
- Handles squash merges scenario

**Transcript Reading Path:**
- Uses `store.ReadLatestSessionContent()` to get transcript
- Falls back to `checkRemoteMetadata()` if local metadata unavailable

### 9. **Read Paths for Status/Explain/Session Commands**

**`entire explain` command:**
- Lists checkpoints via `strategy.listCheckpoints()` → `store.ListCommitted()`
- Explains specific checkpoint: `store.ReadLatestSessionContent()` for transcript/metadata

## Comprehensive Checkpoint System Architecture Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the Entire CLI codebase, here's a detailed understanding of the current checkpoint system:

### 1. **Checkpoint Storage Layer** (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`)

**Core Types & Interfaces:**
- `Store` interface (in `checkpoint.go`) - abstracts read/write operations for both temporary and committed checkpoints
- `GitStore` - implements the Store interface, wrapping a git.Repository
- Two checkpoint types: `Temporary` (shadow branches) and `Committed` (entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)

**Temporary Checkpoints (Shadow Branches):**
- Location: Shadow branches named `entire/<base-commit-short-hash>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
- Used for intra-session rewind
- Written by `WriteTemporary()` in `temporary.go`
- Contain full state: code + metadata in git tree
- Deduplication: skipped if tree hash matches previous checkpoint
- Include worktree ID hash to support multiple worktrees per repo

**Committed Checkpoints (`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch):**
- Location: Sharded paths `<checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/`
- Contain metadata + commit reference
- Written by `WriteCommitted()` in `committed.go`
- Multi-session support: sessions stored in numbered subdirectories (0/, 1/, 2/, etc.)
- Structure per checkpoint:
  ```
  <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
  ├── metadata.json         # CheckpointSummary (aggregated stats)
  ├── 1/                    # First session
  │   ├── metadata.json     # CommittedMetadata (session-specific)
  │   ├── full.jsonl        # Transcript (chunked if large)
  │   ├── prompt.txt        # User prompts
  │   └── content_hash.txt  # SHA256 of transcript
  ├── 2/                    # Second session
  └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/  # Task checkpoints (optional)
      ├── checkpoint.json
      └── agent-<id>.jsonl
  ```

### 2. **Condensation Logic** (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go`)

**CondenseSession Function:**
- Converts temporary checkpoint (shadow branch) → committed checkpoint (metadata branch)
- Checkpoint ID: 12-hex-char stable identifier from `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
- Process:
  1. Extracts session data from shadow branch or live transcript
  2. Filters files_touched to only committed files (1:1 model)
  3. Calculates attribution (agent vs human lines)
  4. Generates AI summary if enabled
  5. Writes to `entire/checkpoints/v1` via `store.WriteCommitted()`

**Data Extraction:**
- `extractSessionData()` - reads from shadow branch tree
- `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript()` - reads live file for mid-session commits
- Falls back to live file if shadow branch is stale
- Handles agent-specific transcript formats (JSONL for Claude Code, JSON for Gemini/OpenCode)

**Token Usage:**
- Calculated at condensation time from transcript portion (CheckpointTranscriptStart)
- Backfilled from full transcript for agents like Copilot CLI that write post-hook

**Prompts:**
- Source of truth: `prompt.txt` in shadow branch
- Fallback: read from filesystem session metadata
- Fallback: extracted from transcript if neither exists

### 3. **Push Logic** (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go`)

**PrePush Hook:**
- Called before pushing to remote
- Pushes two branches:
  1. `entire/checkpoints/v1` - metadata (to checkpoint_remote if configured)
  2. `entire/trails/v1` - trail metadata (always to user's push remote)
- Settings:
  - `push_sessions`: false to disable checkpoint pushing
  - `checkpoint_remote`: {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"} for separate repo

### 4. **Transcript Handling**

**Current Approach (Read-as-is):**
- Transcripts are copied as-is from agent session directories
- No parsing/transformation at storage time
- Agent-agnostic for most cases

**Format Support:**
- **Claude Code**: JSONL format (one message per line)
- **Gemini CLI**: JSON with messages array
- **OpenCode**: JSON export format with info + messages
- **Cursor**: JSONL variant
- **Factory AI Droid**: Custom envelope format with normalized parsing
- **External Agents**: Protocol delegates to binary via `ReadTranscript` subcommand

**Transcript Chunking:**
- Large transcripts are split into chunks before storage
- `agent.ChunkTranscript()` - format-aware splitting
- Stored as `full_0.jsonl`, `full_1.jsonl`, etc.
- Agent-specific chunk reassembly via `ReassembleTranscript()`

**Transcript Lifecycle:**
- Stored in shadow branch during session
- Copied to `entire/checkpoints/v1` at condensation

### 5. **Agent Interface** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go`)

**Current strategy_options:**
- `push_sessions: false` - disable checkpoint pushing
- `checkpoint_remote: {"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` - push checkpoints to separate repo

### 8. **Resume Command** (`cmd/entire/cli/resume.go`)

**Functionality:**
- Finds most recent commit with `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
- Resolves checkpoint ID from trailer

**Multi-checkpoint Resolution:**

### 9. **Read Paths for Status/Explain/Session Commands**

**Rollout approach:**

Before I start proposing approaches, I have my first clarifying question:

**Regarding the Entire Transcript Format and agent-specific compaction:**

The RFD specifies that the CLI writes `transcript.jsonl` at condensation time. Currently, each agent has its own transcript format (Claude Code = JSONL, Gemini = JSON with messages array, OpenCode = JSON export, etc.) and the `TranscriptAnalyzer` interface handles agent-specific parsing.

For the compaction to work, each agent needs a "transcript compactor" that converts its native format → Entire Transcript Format. The built-in agents (Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI) can have compaction logic implemented in Go.

**For external agents (plugins):** The current plugin protocol delegates `ReadTranscript`, `ChunkTranscript`, `ExtractPrompts`, `CalculateTokens` to the external binary. There are two approaches for compaction:

1. **Add a `compact-transcript` subcommand** to the external agent protocol — the plugin binary does the compaction and returns Entire Transcript Format JSONL.
2. **Use a "best-effort" generic compactor** — since external agents already implement `ExtractPrompts` and the transcript is just JSONL/JSON, try to extract user/assistant turns generically and fall back to storing `full.jsonl` only (no compact format) if the format isn't understood.

Which approach do you prefer? Or should we defer external agent compaction support to a later phase entirely (meaning external agents would initially only get `full.jsonl` written, not `transcript.jsonl`)?

content.text:
Good questions — let me address both.

## External Agent Compaction Protocol Extension

Here's a concrete proposal for the plugin protocol:

**New capability:** `"compact_transcript"` declared in the `info` response.

**New subcommand: `compact-transcript`**

```
entire-agent-<name> compact-transcript --session-ref <ref>
```

Input (stdin):
```json
{
  "transcript": "<raw transcript bytes, base64-encoded>",
  "format_version": 1
}
```

Output (stdout):
```json
{
  "entries": "<Entire Transcript Format JSONL, base64-encoded>",
  "assets": [
    {"name": "img-001.png", "data": "<base64>", "media_type": "image/png"}
  ]
}
```

**Fallback behavior:** If the plugin doesn't declare `compact_transcript` capability, the CLI writes `full.jsonl` to `/main` instead of `transcript.jsonl` for that checkpoint. This means:
- Old plugins continue working without changes
- New plugins opt into compaction when ready
- The API/CLI read path checks for `transcript.jsonl` first, falls back to `full.jsonl`

**Why base64 for both directions:** Transcripts can contain arbitrary binary data (images) and multi-byte characters. Base64 avoids JSON encoding issues. This matches the pattern already used for `read-transcript`.

**Why pass the raw transcript via stdin rather than just the session-ref:** The CLI may already have the transcript in memory (just read it for the shadow branch). Passing it avoids a redundant filesystem read by the plugin binary. The `--session-ref` is still provided for context (e.g., if the plugin needs to read additional session metadata).

---

## Parallelizing v2 Migration and Compaction

Yes — this can be cleanly split. The key insight is that `/main` doesn't *need* `transcript.jsonl` from day one. Here's the structure:

**Workstream A: v2 Storage Infrastructure (refs + dual-write + read paths)**
- Implement the `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/` ref structure
- Dual-write: continue writing v1 branch AND write to v2 refs
- Initially, `/main` stores only **metadata** (`metadata.json`, `prompt.txt`, `content_hash.txt`) — no transcript
- `/full/current` stores `full.jsonl` (raw transcript, same as today)
- Update all CLI read paths (`explain`, `resume`, `status`, `rewind`, `doctor`, `clean`) to read from v2 refs with v1 fallback
- Implement generation rotation for `/full/current`
- Update push logic for custom refs under `refs/entire/`
- Implement the v1→v2 migration path

**Workstream B: Transcript Compaction (Entire Transcript Format + agent compactors)**
- Define and implement the Entire Transcript Format types
- Implement compactors for each built-in agent (Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI)
- Add `compact-transcript` to the external agent protocol
- Binary asset externalization logic
- Integration: wire compaction into the condensation path so `transcript.jsonl` is written to `/main`

**The interface between the two workstreams** is small and well-defined:
- Workstream A provides a `WriteToMain(checkpointID, entries map[string][]byte)` capability that accepts arbitrary file entries for a checkpoint
- Workstream B produces `transcript.jsonl` and `assets/*` and calls that same write path
- Until B is ready, A just doesn't write a transcript to `/main` — the read paths know to fall back to `/full/current` for the raw transcript

**The merge point** is when B's compaction output gets wired into A's condensation path. That's a single integration PR after both sides are tested independently.

---

My next question: **Regarding the dual-write transition period and the "shippable at every PR" constraint:**

During the transition, the CLI needs to write to both v1 and v2. Your notes say "start switching dual writing v1 + v2" and "switch over main ref first." I want to make sure I understand the intended rollout sequence:

1. **Phase 1 — Dual-write (v1 + v2):** Every condensation writes to both `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch AND `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*` refs. Read paths prefer v2, fall back to v1. This is behind a strategy option (e.g., `"checkpoints_v2": true`).

2. **Phase 2 — v2 only:** Once validated, stop writing to v1. New installs default to v2. Existing repos auto-migrate on first write (or explicit `entire migrate`).

3. **Phase 3 — v1 cleanup:** Migration tool to convert old v1 data. Eventually remove v1 code paths.

Is that roughly the rollout sequence you had in mind? And specifically: during dual-write, should the v2 refs be **pushed** to remotes, or should pushing v2 refs only happen after we've validated the format in test repos? (This ties into your constraint about not pushing v2 to production repos before validation.)

# External Agent Protocol Specification

## Transcript Access Pattern

The protocol uses a **session reference** (`session-ref`) parameter to locate transcripts. As documented: `"read-transcript --session-ref <path>"` reads a transcript file and returns raw bytes on stdout.

Transcripts are agent-specific files stored in the agent's session directory. The `resolve-session-file` subcommand maps a session ID to its physical location using two parameters: `--session-dir <dir>` and `--session-id <id>`.

## Key Subcommands for Transcript Handling

**Reading:** The plugin receives a file path via command-line argument and outputs raw bytes to stdout. No stdin is required for this operation.

**Chunking:** `chunk-transcript --max-size <n>` accepts raw transcript bytes on stdin and returns JSON: `{"chunks": ["<base64-encoded-chunk>", "..."]}`. This enables storing large transcripts across multiple chunks.

**Reassembly:** The inverse operation accepts chunked data as JSON input on stdin and outputs reconstructed bytes to stdout.

**Position tracking:** `get-transcript-position --path <path>` returns the current byte offset: `{"position": 12345}`. This enables incremental reading.

## stdin/stdout vs Filesystem Access

The protocol follows this pattern:

- **Command parameters** pass filesystem paths and configuration (e.g., `--session-ref`, `--max-size`)
- **Data transfer** uses stdin for input and stdout for output (JSON or raw bytes depending on context)
- **Plugins manage storage**: as noted, `"The plugin is responsible for choosing the storage location and format"` during session persistence

The 30-second timeout and 10 MB output cap apply per invocation, requiring careful design for large transcripts.

## Required vs Optional Capabilities

All plugins must implement core subcommands like `info`, `detect`, `read-session`, and `write-session`. Optional capabilities (e.g., `transcript_analyzer`, `token_calculator`) declare which additional subcommands the plugin supports, preventing unnecessary CLI calls.
